name: Iman
milestone_by_age_26: Discovered by American photographer Peter Beard in 1975 (age 20) while studying at the University of Nairobi; her first modeling assignment was for Vogue in 1976 (age 21), launching a career that made her one of the world's most iconic supermodels.
starting_point: Born in 1955 in Mogadishu, Somalia, to a Somali family; her father was a diplomat and former Somali ambassador to Saudi Arabia, and she grew up in a privileged household before political upheaval led her to flee as a refugee to Kenya.
current_position: Widow of David Bowie (died 2016); philanthropist and founder of Iman Cosmetics; resides in New York; net worth estimated at ~$25 million.

trajectory.title: Birth in Mogadishu
trajectory.description: Born Zara Mohamed Abdulmajid on July 25, 1955, in Mogadishu, Somalia, into a prominent family; her father was a diplomat and former Somali ambassador to Saudi Arabia.

trajectory.title: University of Nairobi
trajectory.description: Enrolled at the University of Nairobi to study political science, working as a translator to help pay tuition after fleeing political instability in Somalia.

trajectory.title: Discovered by Peter Beard
trajectory.description: Discovered by American photographer Peter Beard on a street in Nairobi; he photographed her and took the images to New York, eventually convincing her to move to the US to model.

trajectory.title: First Vogue assignment
trajectory.description: Shot her first editorial spread for American Vogue with photographer Arthur Elgort, launching her modeling career after signing with Wilhelmina Models.

trajectory.title: Revlon campaign and early fame
trajectory.description: Starred in Revlon's Polished Ambers campaign, the first Black woman-centered Revlon campaign, and became a muse for Yves Saint Laurent, Versace, and other top designers.

trajectory.title: Retirement from full-time modeling
trajectory.description: Retired from full-time modeling as a new generation of supermodels (Linda, Christy, Naomi, Cindy) emerged, pivoting toward business and acting.

trajectory.title: Marriage to David Bowie
trajectory.description: Married musician David Bowie in a private ceremony, becoming one of the most celebrated couples in fashion and music.

trajectory.title: Launch of Iman Cosmetics
trajectory.description: Founded Iman Cosmetics, a makeup and skincare line designed for women of color, filling a major gap in the beauty market and growing into a multi-million dollar business.

trajectory.title: CFDA Fashion Icon Award
trajectory.description: Honored with the Fashion Icon Award by the CFDA in recognition of her decades-long influence on the fashion industry and advocacy for diversity.

name: Vassily Ivanchuk
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1988 New York Open at age 19 (ahead of a field of grandmasters), was awarded the Grandmaster title in 1988, tied for first at the World Junior Chess Championship, and won the elite Linares super-tournament in 1989 at age 20.
starting_point: Born in 1969 in Kopychyntsi, a small town in western Ukraine (then Ukrainian SSR); his father was a lawyer and his mother a physics teacher who nurtured his early intellectual development.
current_position: Active Ukrainian chess grandmaster; ranked in the world top 100 as of 2025 with a FIDE rating around 2634; resides in Ukraine.

trajectory.title: Birth in Kopychyntsi
trajectory.description: Born March 18, 1969, in Kopychyntsi, Ukrainian SSR; his father, a lawyer, bought him a magnetic chess set as a birthday gift, sparking his lifelong passion for the game.

trajectory.title: USSR Junior Champion
trajectory.description: Won the USSR Junior Chess Championship and earned bronze in the Ukrainian Chess Championship, marking his emergence as a promising young talent.

trajectory.title: European Junior Champion and IM title
trajectory.description: Won the European Junior Chess Championship in Groningen and was awarded the International Master title by FIDE.

trajectory.title: New York Open and Grandmaster title
trajectory.description: Won the 1988 New York Open with 7.5/9 ahead of a field of grandmasters, tied for first at the World Junior Championship in Adelaide, and was awarded the Grandmaster title, entering the world top 10.

trajectory.title: Linares super-tournament victory
trajectory.description: Won the elite Linares super-tournament, cementing his reputation as one of the world's most talented and unpredictable players.

trajectory.title: World No. 2 ranking
trajectory.description: Reached No. 2 on the FIDE world rankings for the first time, a position he would hold on three separate occasions (1991, 1992, 2007).

trajectory.title: FIDE World Championship final
trajectory.description: Reached the final of the 2002 FIDE World Chess Championship, losing to Ruslan Ponomariov in a closely contested match.

trajectory.title: World Blitz Champion
trajectory.description: Won the FIDE World Blitz Chess Championship, showcasing his exceptional speed chess abilities and reaching a peak rating of 2787.

trajectory.title: World Rapid Champion
trajectory.description: Won the FIDE World Rapid Chess Championship, adding another world title to his already distinguished career spanning three decades.

name: Dikembe Mutombo
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 4th overall in the 1991 NBA draft at age 25 and named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 1992; was a 2x Big East Defensive Player of the Year and All-American at Georgetown by age 25.
starting_point: Born in 1966 in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, to a large family; his father was a school headmaster. He grew up aspiring to become a doctor and did not start playing basketball until age 16.
current_position: Died September 30, 2024, at age 58 from brain cancer; final role: NBA global ambassador and philanthropist who built a hospital in Kinshasa.

trajectory.title: Birth in Kinshasa
trajectory.description: Born June 25, 1966, in Kinshasa, DRC, one of ten children; his father was a school headmaster and he grew up with aspirations of becoming a doctor.

trajectory.title: Georgetown University arrival
trajectory.description: Moved to Washington, D.C. to attend Georgetown University on an academic scholarship, initially planning to study medicine before coach John Thompson recruited him to basketball.

trajectory.title: Big East Defensive Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Named Big East Defensive Player of the Year for the second time and earned All-American honors at Georgetown, establishing himself as the premier defensive center in college basketball.

trajectory.title: NBA Draft 4th overall
trajectory.description: Selected 4th overall by the Denver Nuggets in the 1991 NBA Draft, making an immediate impact as a dominant defensive force.

trajectory.title: NBA All-Rookie First Team
trajectory.description: Named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team after averaging 16.6 points, 12.3 rebounds, and nearly 3 blocks per game in his debut season.

trajectory.title: First NBA Defensive Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Won the first of four NBA Defensive Player of the Year awards, leading the league in blocked shots and becoming the signature defensive anchor of his era.

trajectory.title: NBA All-Star with Atlanta Hawks
trajectory.description: Selected to his eighth and final NBA All-Star Game while playing for the Atlanta Hawks, capping a dominant defensive career.

trajectory.title: NBA retirement
trajectory.description: Retired after 18 NBA seasons with 3,289 career blocks, the second most in NBA history at the time, having played for the Nuggets, Hawks, 76ers, Nets, Knicks, and Rockets.

trajectory.title: Death from brain cancer
trajectory.description: Died September 30, 2024, at age 58, remembered as one of the greatest defensive players in NBA history and a dedicated philanthropist who funded a hospital in Kinshasa.

name: John Walker
milestone_by_age_26: Ran his first sub-four-minute mile in July 1973 (age 21), broke the world mile record with 3:49.4 in August 1975 (age 23) becoming the first man under 3:50, and won Olympic 1500m gold at the 1976 Montreal Games (age 24).
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Papakura, New Zealand, to a working-class family; he grew up in a rural setting and began running cross-country at Manurewa Normal School before being coached by Arch Jelley using the Arthur Lydiard training method.
current_position: Retired former middle-distance runner; served as Auckland Councillor representing the Manurewa-Papakura ward; knighted in 2009 as Sir John Walker; lives in New Zealand.

trajectory.title: Birth in Papakura
trajectory.description: Born January 12, 1952, in Papakura, New Zealand, into a working-class family in a rural area south of Auckland.

trajectory.title: National 800m breakthrough
trajectory.description: Won his first New Zealand senior title in the 800m at the Tauranga New Year's Day meet, defeating national champion Dick Quax, but narrowly missed qualifying for the Munich Olympics.

trajectory.title: First sub-four-minute mile
trajectory.description: Ran his first sub-four-minute mile in July 1973, establishing himself as a serious international middle-distance contender.

trajectory.title: Commonwealth Games silver
trajectory.description: Won silver in the 1500m at the Christchurch Commonwealth Games in one of the greatest 1500m races ever, with both Walker and winner Filbert Bayi breaking the world record.

trajectory.title: World mile record — first under 3:50
trajectory.description: Broke the world mile record with 3:49.4 in Gothenburg, Sweden on August 12, 1975, becoming the first man in history to run under 3:50 for the mile.

trajectory.title: Olympic 1500m gold
trajectory.description: Won the gold medal in the men's 1500m at the Montreal Olympics, becoming the third New Zealander to win that prestigious event.

trajectory.title: 100 sub-four-minute miles
trajectory.description: Became the first athlete in history to achieve 100 sub-four-minute miles, a milestone of extraordinary consistency and longevity in middle-distance running.

trajectory.title: Knighthood
trajectory.description: Knighted by Queen Elizabeth II to become Sir John Walker, recognizing his contributions to New Zealand athletics and public service.

name: Sócrates
milestone_by_age_26: Began playing professionally for Botafogo-SP in 1974 at age 20, was named revelation (newcomer) of the Campeonato Paulista that year, and was the tournament's top scorer in 1976 at age 22.
starting_point: Born in 1954 in Belém, Brazil, to an educated family; his father was passionate about literature and named him after the Greek philosopher. He pursued a medical degree while playing football, an unusual combination that earned him the nickname 'Doctor Socrates.'
current_position: Died December 4, 2011, at age 57 from septic shock; final role: football commentator and columnist, having also practiced medicine briefly.

trajectory.title: Birth in Belém
trajectory.description: Born February 19, 1954, in Belém, Pará, Brazil; his father, inspired by Plato's Republic, named him after the Greek philosopher Sócrates and nurtured his intellectual curiosity.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Botafogo-SP
trajectory.description: Began playing professionally for Botafogo-SP in Ribeirão Preto, was named revelation of the Campeonato Paulista, and balanced football with his medical studies.

trajectory.title: Campeonato Paulista top scorer
trajectory.description: Became the top scorer of the Campeonato Paulista with 15 goals, including seven in a single match against Portuguesa Santista, drawing attention from major clubs.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Corinthians
trajectory.description: Signed for Corinthians after completing his medical degree, becoming a pillar of one of the most historic teams in Brazilian club football.

trajectory.title: Brazil captain at World Cup
trajectory.description: Captained Brazil's iconic 1982 World Cup squad, known for its beautiful attacking football, scoring four goals in the tournament and becoming a symbol of the 'jogo bonito' era.

trajectory.title: South American Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named South American Footballer of the Year, recognizing his status as one of the continent's premier players and leading Corinthians to the São Paulo state championship.

trajectory.title: Move to Fiorentina
trajectory.description: Transferred to Fiorentina in Italy's Serie A, spending one season in European football before returning to Brazil.

trajectory.title: FIFA 100 selection
trajectory.description: Named by Pelé to the FIFA 100 list of the world's greatest living players, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest midfielders of all time.

trajectory.title: Death in São Paulo
trajectory.description: Died December 4, 2011, at age 57 from septic shock, remembered as the 'Doctor' who combined intellectual depth with extraordinary footballing talent.

name: Aleksandr Karelin
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in Greco-Roman super-heavyweight wrestling at the 1988 Seoul Olympics at age 21, having become world junior champion in 1987 and earned a place on the Soviet national team.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Novosibirsk, Siberia, USSR; he was a remarkably large baby (6.8 kg at birth) and began wrestling at age 13 under coach Viktor Kuznetsov, who remained his sole coach throughout his career.
current_position: Russian politician and retired wrestler; serves as a State Duma deputy; widely regarded as the greatest Greco-Roman wrestler of all time; lives in Russia.

trajectory.title: Birth in Novosibirsk
trajectory.description: Born September 19, 1967, in Novosibirsk, Siberia, weighing an extraordinary 6.8 kg (15 lbs) at birth; showed early aptitude for literature and mathematics in school.

trajectory.title: Began wrestling training
trajectory.description: Started training in Greco-Roman wrestling under Viktor Kuznetsov, who remained his coach for his entire career, initially trying boxing and weightlifting before committing to wrestling.

trajectory.title: World Junior Champion
trajectory.description: Won the World Junior Championships and earned a place on the Soviet national team, having also won the European Junior Championships in 1986.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold in Seoul
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold in Greco-Roman super-heavyweight wrestling at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, beginning an unprecedented era of dominance in the sport.

trajectory.title: Second Olympic gold
trajectory.description: Defended his Olympic title at the 1992 Barcelona Games competing for the Unified Team, remaining undefeated between Seoul and Barcelona.

trajectory.title: Third consecutive Olympic gold
trajectory.description: Won his third consecutive Olympic gold at the 1996 Atlanta Games, becoming the first wrestler to win the same weight class three times, outscoring his five opponents 25-0.

trajectory.title: Elected to State Duma
trajectory.description: Elected to the Russian State Duma, beginning a political career while still competing at the highest level of wrestling.

trajectory.title: Olympic silver and retirement
trajectory.description: Lost 1-0 to American Rulon Gardner in the 2000 Sydney Olympic final, ending a 13-year undefeated streak; retired with 887 wins and 2 losses, considered the greatest Greco-Roman wrestler ever.

name: Guillermo Vilas
milestone_by_age_26: Won the year-end Masters Grand Prix title in 1974 at age 22, defeating Björn Borg and Ilie Năstase, and finished in the year-end top ten for the first time, establishing himself as a major contender.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Buenos Aires, Argentina, to a middle-class family; he was a published poet and intellectual who brought an artistic sensibility to tennis, earning the nickname 'Young Bull of the Pampas.'
current_position: Retired former professional tennis player; inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 1991; resides in Monaco; widely regarded as Argentina's greatest tennis player.

trajectory.title: Birth in Buenos Aires
trajectory.description: Born August 17, 1952, in Buenos Aires, Argentina; developed a love for literature and poetry alongside tennis, becoming a published author and intellectual figure in the sport.

trajectory.title: Turned professional
trajectory.description: Turned professional in 1968, beginning a career that would span 24 years and see him become the foremost Latin American male tennis player of his era.

trajectory.title: First ATP title
trajectory.description: Won his first ATP singles title in Buenos Aires, defeating Björn Borg in the final, signaling his arrival as a serious contender on the international tour.

trajectory.title: Masters Grand Prix title
trajectory.description: Won the year-end Masters Grand Prix title, defeating Björn Borg and Ilie Năstase, and finished in the year-end top ten for the first time.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough year — French and US Open titles
trajectory.description: Won the French Open and US Open singles titles, compiled a 46-match winning streak, and won 17 of 33 tournaments entered, with 145 match wins against 14 losses in one of the greatest seasons in tennis history.

trajectory.title: Australian Open champion
trajectory.description: Won the Australian Open singles title, adding a third Grand Slam to his collection and solidifying his status as one of the world's premier players.

trajectory.title: Second Australian Open title
trajectory.description: Won the Australian Open for a second consecutive year, bringing his Grand Slam singles total to four titles.

trajectory.title: International Tennis Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, recognized as the first Argentine to win major titles and a trailblazer for Latin American tennis.

name: Roberto Carlos
milestone_by_age_26: Called up for the Brazil national team in 1992 at age 19, won two consecutive Brazilian league titles with Palmeiras (1993 and 1994, ages 20-21), joined Inter Milan in 1995 (age 22) and Real Madrid in 1996 (age 23), becoming their first-choice left-back; by age 26 (1999) he was a World Cup runner-up (1998) and established as one of the world's best left-backs.
starting_point: Born in 1973 in Garça, São Paulo, Brazil, to a poor family; he worked at a textile factory as a 12-year-old to help support his family before starting his football career at União São João at age 16.
current_position: Retired former professional footballer; works as a football ambassador and commentator; resides in Brazil; net worth estimated at ~$160 million.

trajectory.title: Birth in Garça, São Paulo
trajectory.description: Born April 10, 1973, in Garça, São Paulo, Brazil, to a poor family; worked at a textile factory as a child to help support his family before joining União São João's youth academy.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at União São João
trajectory.description: Began his professional career at União São João, initially as a forward before converting to left-back, and was loaned to Atlético Mineiro in 1992.

trajectory.title: Brazil national team call-up
trajectory.description: Called up for the Brazil national team for the first time at age 19, representing Brazil at the 1992 Olympics and in Copa América.

trajectory.title: Palmeiras and Brazilian league titles
trajectory.description: Signed for Palmeiras and won two consecutive Brazilian league titles (1993 and 1994), forming an exceptional left wing partnership with Rivaldo.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Inter Milan
trajectory.description: Joined Inter Milan in a £4.5 million deal, spending one season in Serie A before being signed by Real Madrid.

trajectory.title: Real Madrid transfer
trajectory.description: Joined Real Madrid under Fabio Capello, immediately becoming their first-choice left-back and beginning an 11-season tenure at the club.

trajectory.title: Famous free-kick vs France
trajectory.description: Scored an iconic free-kick against France in the Tournoi de France 1997 with an impossible curve, widely considered one of the greatest free-kicks ever scored.

trajectory.title: World Cup runner-up
trajectory.description: Reached the World Cup final with Brazil at France 1998, establishing himself as one of the world's best left-backs on the global stage.

trajectory.title: Champions League and World Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won his third Champions League with Real Madrid and was a key member of Brazil's 2002 World Cup-winning squad, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest full-backs in history.

trajectory.title: Departure from Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Left Real Madrid after 11 seasons, 584 appearances, and 71 goals, having won four La Liga titles and three Champions League trophies, then joined Fenerbahçe.

name: Evonne Goolagong Cawley
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1971 French Open at age 19 on debut, followed by the 1971 Wimbledon title, and went on to win multiple Australian Open titles (1974, 1975, 1976, 1977) and reach World No. 1 by 1976, all before age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1951 in Griffith, New South Wales, Australia, as the third of eight children in a Wiradjuri Aboriginal family; her father was a sheep shearer and her mother a homemaker. The townsfolk of Barellan raised funds to help her travel to tournaments.
current_position: Retired former professional tennis player; serves as a tennis ambassador and mentor for Indigenous Australian youth; resides in Australia; inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 1988.

trajectory.title: Birth in Griffith, NSW
trajectory.description: Born July 31, 1951, in Griffith, New South Wales, the third of eight children in a Wiradjuri Aboriginal family; her father was a sheep shearer and her mother a homemaker.

trajectory.title: Move to Sydney for training
trajectory.description: Talent-spotted by Sydney-based coach Vic Edwards, moved to Sydney with her parents' blessing to pursue professional tennis training, using a piece of wood from a fruit packing box as her first racquet.

trajectory.title: French Open and Wimbledon champion
trajectory.description: Won the French Open singles on debut and the Wimbledon singles title, becoming the second woman in the Open Era to complete the Channel Slam and the first Indigenous Australian to win a Grand Slam.

trajectory.title: First of four consecutive Australian Open titles
trajectory.description: Won the first of four consecutive Australian Open singles titles (1974-1977), establishing dominance at her home Grand Slam.

trajectory.title: World No. 1 ranking
trajectory.description: Reached World No. 1 on the WTA rankings on April 26, 1976, though formal recognition of her two-week reign was delayed until 2007 due to a computing error.

trajectory.title: Second Wimbledon title as a mother
trajectory.description: Won Wimbledon for a second time, becoming the first mother to win the title in 66 years and capping a remarkable career comeback.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional tennis
trajectory.description: Retired from professional tennis with 86 WTA singles titles, seven Grand Slam singles titles, and a career record of 704-165.

trajectory.title: International Tennis Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, recognized as one of the greatest players of the 1970s and a trailblazer for Indigenous athletes worldwide.

name: Jody Scheckter
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 1974 Swedish Grand Prix at age 24, becoming the first South African to win an F1 race, and was a championship contender that same year.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in East London, South Africa, to a family with automotive ties; his father owned a Renault dealership where Jody worked as an engineering apprentice and learned to drive at a young age.
current_position: Retired former racing driver and businessman; runs an organic farm in Hampshire, England; remains the only African driver to have won the F1 World Championship.

trajectory.title: Birth in East London, South Africa
trajectory.description: Born January 29, 1950, in East London, Cape Province, South Africa; his father owned a Renault dealership where Jody worked as an engineering apprentice and developed his passion for motorsport.

trajectory.title: South African Formula Ford champion
trajectory.description: Won the South African Formula Ford series and the Driver to Europe scholarship, using the prize money to move to England and pursue a professional racing career.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut with McLaren
trajectory.description: Made his Formula One debut at the United States Grand Prix driving for McLaren, having raced in British and European Formula Two that year.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory at Swedish Grand Prix
trajectory.description: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 1974 Swedish Grand Prix with Tyrrell, becoming the first South African to win an F1 race and finishing third in the championship.

trajectory.title: Six-wheeled Tyrrell P34 victory
trajectory.description: Won the Swedish Grand Prix driving the unique six-wheeled Tyrrell P34, remaining the only driver ever to win a Grand Prix on six wheels.

trajectory.title: Championship runner-up with Wolf
trajectory.description: Finished runner-up to Niki Lauda in the 1977 World Championship driving for Wolf, winning several races including the Monaco Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: F1 World Champion with Ferrari
trajectory.description: Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Ferrari, becoming the first and only African driver to win the title, clinching it with victory at the Italian Grand Prix at Monza.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Formula One
trajectory.description: Retired from Formula One at the end of the 1980 season after Ferrari struggled with the uncompetitive 312T5, ending his career with 10 race wins and the 1979 world title.

name: Claudia Schiffer
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved breakthrough as the face of Guess campaigns in 1989 at age 19, became Chanel's new face in 1990 at 20, and signed a record $6 million/year Revlon contract in 1992 at 22, becoming the highest-paid model in history—all well before 26.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Rheinberg, Germany, to a middle-class family; her father was a lawyer and she originally aspired to join the legal profession, working in her father's law firm before being discovered at 17.
current_position: Retired from full-time modeling; married to film director Matthew Vaughn; net worth estimated at ~$70 million; resides in the UK and Germany.

trajectory.title: Birth in Rheinberg, Germany
trajectory.description: Born August 25, 1970, in Rheinberg, Germany, the oldest of four children; her father was a lawyer and she initially aspired to follow him into the legal profession.

trajectory.title: Discovered in Düsseldorf nightclub
trajectory.description: Scouted at age 17 in a Düsseldorf nightclub by Michel Levaton, CEO of Metropolitan Models, and was signed to the agency, flying to Paris for a trial photo shoot.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with Guess campaigns
trajectory.description: Achieved breakthrough as the face of Guess campaigns, photographed by Ellen von Unwerth, with her resemblance to Brigitte Bardot catapulting her to stardom.

trajectory.title: Chanel's new face
trajectory.description: Became Chanel's new face under Karl Lagerfeld, walking in his fashion shows and appearing on covers of Elle, Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, and Time.

trajectory.title: Record Revlon contract
trajectory.description: Signed a record $6 million per year contract with Revlon, becoming the highest-paid model in history and appearing on over 1,000 magazine covers, a Guinness World Record.

trajectory.title: Film career begins
trajectory.description: Ventured into acting with roles in films including Richie Rich and later Love Actually, expanding her career beyond modeling.

trajectory.title: Cashmere collection launch
trajectory.description: Launched her own cashmere fashion collection, transitioning from model to designer and businesswoman.

name: Sudha Murty
milestone_by_age_26: Became the first female engineer hired at India's largest auto manufacturer, TATA Engineering and Locomotive Company (TELCO), in 1974 at age 23-24, after writing a postcard to the chairman challenging the 'men only' hiring policy.
starting_point: Born in 1950 in Shiggaon, Haveri district, Karnataka, India, to a Kannada-speaking family; her father was a surgeon and her mother a schoolteacher, and she was raised with a strong emphasis on education.
current_position: Indian educator, author, and philanthropist; nominated as Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) in March 2024; awarded Padma Bhushan in 2023; resides in Bengaluru, India.

trajectory.title: Birth in Shiggaon, Karnataka
trajectory.description: Born August 19, 1950, in Shiggaon, Haveri district, Karnataka, India, the daughter of a surgeon and a schoolteacher who instilled a deep value for education.

trajectory.title: Engineering studies begin
trajectory.description: Enrolled in B.V.B. College of Engineering & Technology for a BEng in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, becoming the only female student in her engineering class.

trajectory.title: First female engineer at TELCO
trajectory.description: Became the first female engineer hired at TATA Engineering and Locomotive Company (TELCO) after writing a postcard to chairman JRD Tata challenging the 'men only' hiring policy, and was hired after a special interview.

trajectory.title: Marriage to Narayana Murthy
trajectory.description: Married N.R. Narayana Murthy, who co-founded Infosys that same year; she supported the family financially during Infosys's early years with her TELCO salary.

trajectory.title: Founded Infosys Foundation
trajectory.description: Established the Infosys Foundation, serving as its chairperson and building schools, hospitals, and orphanages across India, impacting thousands of lives.

trajectory.title: Padma Shri award
trajectory.description: Awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, for her contributions to social work and philanthropy.

trajectory.title: Padma Bhushan award
trajectory.description: Awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award, recognizing her extensive philanthropic work and literary contributions.

trajectory.title: Nominated to Rajya Sabha
trajectory.description: Nominated as Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, on March 8, 2024, for her contributions to social work and education.

name: Javier Sotomayor
milestone_by_age_26: Set world junior record at 2.33m at age 16 (May 1984) and first senior world record at 2.43m at age 20 (September 1988), becoming the first person to clear 8 feet in 1989.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Limonar, Matanzas, Cuba, a small town 150km west of Havana; he was scouted by basketball coaches due to his height but was steered toward high jump, beginning athletics in 1978.
current_position: Retired Cuban track and field athlete; remains the world record holder in the high jump at 2.45m; lives in Cuba.

trajectory.title: Birth in Limonar, Cuba
trajectory.description: Born October 13, 1967, in Limonar, Matanzas, Cuba; was scouted by basketball coaches for his height but was steered toward high jump, beginning athletics training in 1978.

trajectory.title: World junior record at 2.33m
trajectory.description: Set the world junior record of 2.33m in Havana in May 1984, but was unable to compete at the Los Angeles Olympics due to Cuba's boycott of the Games.

trajectory.title: First senior world record at 2.43m
trajectory.description: Set his first senior world record of 2.43m in Salamanca, Spain in September 1988, but missed the Seoul Olympics due to another Cuban boycott.

trajectory.title: First person to clear 8 feet
trajectory.description: Became the first and only person ever to clear 8 feet (2.44m) in the high jump, a historic milestone in athletics.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold in Barcelona
trajectory.description: Won the Olympic gold medal in the high jump at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, the pinnacle achievement of his career.

trajectory.title: Current world record of 2.45m
trajectory.description: Set the current world record of 2.45m (8 ft 1/4 in) in Salamanca, Spain on July 27, 1993, a record that still stands today.

trajectory.title: Retirement from athletics
trajectory.description: Retired from high-level competition after a 23-year career, having won seven world crowns, Olympic gold, and set five world records.

name: Vlade Divac
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Yugoslavia senior national team at the 1986 FIBA World Championship at age 18 and won gold at the 1987 FIBA Junior World Championship; was an established NBA player with the Lakers by age 24.
starting_point: Born in 1968 in Prijepolje, SR Serbia, SFR Yugoslavia; he began playing basketball for his hometown team KK Elan before moving to Sloga Kraljevo as a teenager.
current_position: Former NBA executive and player; served as Vice President of Basketball Operations and GM of the Sacramento Kings; President of the Serbian Olympic Committee (2009-2017); resides in Serbia.

trajectory.title: Birth in Prijepolje
trajectory.description: Born February 3, 1968, in Prijepolje, SR Serbia, SFR Yugoslavia; began playing basketball for his hometown team KK Elan before joining Sloga Kraljevo.

trajectory.title: Yugoslavia senior national team debut
trajectory.description: Debuted for the Yugoslavia senior national team at the 1986 FIBA World Championship, beginning an international career that would span 145 appearances.

trajectory.title: FIBA Junior World Championship gold
trajectory.description: Won gold at the 1987 FIBA Junior World Championship with Yugoslavia, part of a golden generation of Yugoslav basketball.

trajectory.title: NBA Draft and Lakers debut
trajectory.description: Selected 26th overall by the Los Angeles Lakers in the 1989 NBA Draft, becoming one of the first European players to make a significant impact in the NBA.

trajectory.title: Trade to Charlotte Hornets
trajectory.description: Traded from the Lakers to the Charlotte Hornets in the same deal that brought Kobe Bryant to Los Angeles, spending two productive seasons in Charlotte.

trajectory.title: Sacramento Kings era begins
trajectory.description: Signed with the Sacramento Kings, becoming a central figure in one of the most exciting teams of the early 2000s alongside Chris Webber and Peja Stojaković.

trajectory.title: NBA All-Star
trajectory.description: Selected to his only NBA All-Star Game, recognizing his exceptional passing ability and all-around play as a center.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional basketball
trajectory.description: Retired after 16 NBA seasons with over 13,000 points, 9,000 rebounds, 3,000 assists, and 1,600 blocked shots, one of the greatest all-around European players in NBA history.

name: Patrick Swayze
milestone_by_age_26: Made Broadway debut in Goodtime Charley (1976) at age 24 and won the leading role of Danny Zuko in the Broadway production of Grease (1978) at age 25, which led to film and television offers.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Houston, Texas, to a dance-oriented family; his mother, Patsy Swayze, was director of the Houston Jazz Ballet Company and introduced him to dance at an early age, while his father was an engineering drafter.
current_position: Died September 14, 2009, at age 57 from pancreatic cancer; final role: starred in the TV series The Beast (2009).

trajectory.title: Birth in Houston, Texas
trajectory.description: Born August 18, 1952, in Houston, Texas, to Patsy Swayze, a choreographer and dance instructor, and Jesse Wayne Swayze, an engineering drafter; his mother introduced him to dance early.

trajectory.title: Move to New York for dance
trajectory.description: Moved to New York City to pursue a dance career, training at the Harkness and Joffrey Ballet companies before joining the Eliot Feld Ballet Company as a principal dancer.

trajectory.title: Broadway debut in Goodtime Charley
trajectory.description: Made his Broadway debut in Goodtime Charley at the Palace Theatre, redirecting his career from pure dance toward stage acting.

trajectory.title: Leading role in Broadway's Grease
trajectory.description: Won the leading role of Danny Zuko in the Broadway production of Grease at the Royale Theatre, which led to numerous film and television offers.

trajectory.title: Film debut in Skatetown, U.S.A.
trajectory.description: Made his film debut as Ace Johnson in Skatetown, U.S.A., capitalizing on the disco craze and beginning his transition to screen acting.

trajectory.title: The Outsiders breakthrough
trajectory.description: Appeared in Francis Ford Coppola's The Outsiders alongside Tom Cruise, Matt Dillon, and Emilio Estevez, marking his breakthrough into major Hollywood films.

trajectory.title: Dirty Dancing stardom
trajectory.description: Starred as Johnny Castle in Dirty Dancing, a low-budget film that became a massive international hit, earning him a Golden Globe nomination and making him a global star.

trajectory.title: Ghost blockbuster
trajectory.description: Starred in Ghost alongside Demi Moore, which became one of the highest-grossing films of 1990 and solidified his status as a leading man.

trajectory.title: Death from pancreatic cancer
trajectory.description: Died September 14, 2009, at age 57 from pancreatic cancer, having continued working through his illness on the TV series The Beast.

name: Mario Botta
milestone_by_age_26: Designed his first building, a two-family house at Morbio Superiore, at age 16, and by age 26 had apprenticed with Carloni and Camenisch, studied at the Art College in Milan and Iuav in Venice, and worked with renowned architects Le Corbusier, Louis Kahn, and Carlo Scarpa.
starting_point: Born in 1943 in Mendrisio, Ticino, Switzerland, to a modest family in Switzerland's Italian-speaking region; he showed early aptitude for design and left secondary school at age 15 to apprentice as a draughtsman.
current_position: Internationally renowned Swiss architect; founder of Mario Botta Architetti in Mendrisio; co-founder of the Academy of Architecture at USI in Mendrisio; continues to design and teach at age 82.

trajectory.title: Birth in Mendrisio, Switzerland
trajectory.description: Born April 1, 1943, in Mendrisio, Ticino, the Italian-speaking region of Switzerland, into a modest family.

trajectory.title: Apprenticeship and first building design
trajectory.description: Left secondary school at 15 to apprentice as a draughtsman at Carloni and Camenisch architects in Lugano, and designed his first building—a two-family house at Morbio Superiore—at age 16.

trajectory.title: Art College in Milan
trajectory.description: Attended the Art College in Milan for his baccalaureate, developing his artistic and design foundations.

trajectory.title: Work with Le Corbusier
trajectory.description: While studying at IUAV in Venice, worked as a studio assistant for Le Corbusier on the Venice Hospital project, a formative experience with one of modernism's greatest architects.

trajectory.title: IUAV graduation and work with Louis Kahn
trajectory.description: Graduated from the Università Iuav di Venezia with a thesis supervised by Carlo Scarpa, having also worked with Louis Kahn on the Congress Hall project in Venice.

trajectory.title: Founded own architectural practice
trajectory.description: Opened his own architectural firm in Lugano, initially concentrating on single-family houses in Ticino that would define his stark, geometric style.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Academy of Architecture
trajectory.description: Co-founded the Academy of Architecture of the Università della Svizzera Italiana in Mendrisio, serving as one of its first directors and shaping a new generation of architects.

name: Arvydas Sabonis
milestone_by_age_26: Won three consecutive Soviet Premier League championships with Žalgiris (1985-1987) and the 1986 FIBA Club World Cup, while also being a key member of the Soviet national team from 1982, all by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Kaunas, Lithuania (then Lithuanian SSR, Soviet Union); he grew up in the Soviet basketball system, joining the Žalgiris Kaunas junior team and developing into a 7'3" center with extraordinary passing ability.
current_position: Retired Lithuanian basketball player and businessman; president of Žalgiris Kaunas; widely regarded as one of the greatest European players of all time; resides in Lithuania.

trajectory.title: Birth in Kaunas, Lithuania
trajectory.description: Born December 19, 1964, in Kaunas, Lithuanian SSR, Soviet Union; grew up in the Žalgiris Kaunas junior system, developing into a 7'3" center with exceptional passing and shooting skills.

trajectory.title: Soviet national team debut
trajectory.description: Became a key member of the Soviet national team, beginning an international career that would include multiple Olympic medals.

trajectory.title: First Soviet Premier League championship
trajectory.description: Won the first of three consecutive Soviet Premier League championships with Žalgiris Kaunas (1985-1987) and was named European Player of the Year.

trajectory.title: FIBA Club World Cup and NBA draft
trajectory.description: Won the 1986 FIBA Intercontinental Cup with Žalgiris and was selected by the Portland Trail Blazers in the first round of the 1986 NBA Draft, though he could not immediately leave the USSR.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold with Soviet Union
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold at the 1988 Seoul Olympics with the Soviet Union basketball team, the pinnacle of his international career.

trajectory.title: Move to Spain and Olympic bronze
trajectory.description: Signed with Forum Valladolid in Spain and won Olympic bronze with Lithuania at the 1992 Barcelona Games, representing the newly independent nation.

trajectory.title: EuroLeague champion with Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Won the EuroLeague with Real Madrid, then joined the Portland Trail Blazers in the NBA at age 31, finally making his long-awaited NBA debut.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional basketball
trajectory.description: Retired after a final stint with Žalgiris Kaunas, having won six Euroscar European Player of the Year awards and been named one of FIBA's 50 Greatest Players.

name: Miguel Induráin
milestone_by_age_26: Turned professional in September 1984 at age 20, won his first professional race at the Tour de l'Avenir, became the youngest rider to lead the Vuelta a España in 1985, and won a stage of the Tour de France in 1989, all by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Villava, a village in Navarra, Spain, to a farming family; he grew up in a rural environment and showed exceptional physical attributes, including a resting heart rate of 28 bpm, that would make him a dominant time trialist.
current_position: Retired Spanish road racing cyclist; five-time consecutive Tour de France winner (1991-1995); resides in Navarra, Spain; remains one of cycling's all-time greats.

trajectory.title: Birth in Villava, Navarra
trajectory.description: Born July 16, 1964, in Villava (now Villava-Atarrabia), Navarra, Spain, to a farming family; showed exceptional physical gifts including a remarkably low resting heart rate.

trajectory.title: Turned professional
trajectory.description: Turned professional in September 1984 with the Reynolds team, winning his first professional race at the Tour de l'Avenir.

trajectory.title: Youngest Vuelta a España leader
trajectory.description: Became the youngest rider to wear the leader's jersey at the Vuelta a España, signaling his potential as a future Grand Tour contender.

trajectory.title: First Tour de France stage win
trajectory.description: Won a stage of the Tour de France and won Paris-Nice, establishing himself as a serious contender for Grand Tour general classification.

trajectory.title: First Tour de France victory
trajectory.description: Won his first Tour de France, beginning an unprecedented run of five consecutive victories (1991-1995) in cycling's most prestigious race.

trajectory.title: Giro-Tour double
trajectory.description: Won both the Giro d'Italia and the Tour de France in the same season, becoming one of only seven riders to achieve the Giro-Tour double.

trajectory.title: World Hour Record
trajectory.description: Set the World Hour Record of 53.040 km on September 2, 1994, demonstrating his extraordinary time-trialing power.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold and retirement
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold in the individual time trial at the 1996 Atlanta Games and retired at the end of the season as a five-time Tour de France champion.

name: Lars von Trier
milestone_by_age_26: At age 25, won two Best School Film awards at the Munich International Festival of Film Schools for 'Nocturne' and 'Last Detail,' and had his graduation film 'Images of Liberation' released as a theatrical feature.
starting_point: Born in 1956 in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark, into an intellectual family; his parents were both teachers with Communist and nudist leanings, and he began making films as a child, working on Danish television series from the late 1960s.
current_position: Danish film director and screenwriter; continues to work in film despite health challenges; resides in Denmark; considered one of the most provocative and influential European directors.

trajectory.title: Birth in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark
trajectory.description: Born April 30, 1956, in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark, to intellectual parents who were both teachers; began making films as a child and worked on Danish TV series Secret Summer from the late 1960s.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at National Film School of Denmark
trajectory.description: Enrolled at the National Film School of Denmark after studying film at the University of Copenhagen, beginning his formal filmmaking education.

trajectory.title: Munich Film Festival awards
trajectory.description: Won two Best School Film awards at the Munich International Festival of Film Schools for 'Nocturne' and 'Last Detail,' and had his graduation film 'Images of Liberation' released as a theatrical feature.

trajectory.title: Feature debut with The Element of Crime
trajectory.description: Released his feature debut 'The Element of Crime,' which won the Technical Grand Prize at Cannes and received a Palme d'Or nomination, launching his international career.

trajectory.title: Europa trilogy completed
trajectory.description: Completed the Europa trilogy (The Element of Crime, Epidemic, Europa), establishing his reputation for dark, provocative, and technically innovative filmmaking.

trajectory.title: Dogme 95 manifesto
trajectory.description: Co-created the Dogme 95 filmmaking movement with Thomas Vinterberg, presenting the manifesto in Paris as a protest against superficial, technology-driven cinema.

trajectory.title: Breaking the Waves breakthrough
trajectory.description: Released 'Breaking the Waves,' which won the Grand Prix at Cannes and brought him mainstream international recognition as a major auteur director.

trajectory.title: Palme d'Or for Dancer in the Dark
trajectory.description: Won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for 'Dancer in the Dark,' starring Björk, cementing his status as one of European cinema's most distinctive voices.

name: Luis Enrique
milestone_by_age_26: Made his La Liga debut with Sporting Gijón in September 1989 at age 19, joined Real Madrid in 1991 at age 21, and earned his first cap for Spain in April 1991, establishing himself as a top-flight professional and international by his mid-20s.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Gijón, Asturias, Spain, to a local family; he grew up in his hometown and joined Sporting Gijón's youth academy, earning the nickname 'Lucho' for his combative style.
current_position: Head coach of Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in Ligue 1; one of the most respected football managers in Europe; resides in Paris, France.

trajectory.title: Birth in Gijón, Asturias
trajectory.description: Born May 8, 1970, in Gijón, Asturias, Spain; joined Sporting Gijón's youth academy and developed into a versatile, combative player nicknamed 'Lucho.'

trajectory.title: La Liga debut with Sporting Gijón
trajectory.description: Made his La Liga debut with Sporting Gijón in September 1989, quickly establishing himself as a talented and versatile attacker.

trajectory.title: Real Madrid transfer and Spain debut
trajectory.description: Joined Real Madrid in 1991 and earned his first cap for the Spain national team in April 1991, establishing himself as a top-flight professional and international.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold with Spain
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold with Spain at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, a landmark achievement for Spanish football.

trajectory.title: Controversial move to Barcelona
trajectory.description: Made the controversial move from Real Madrid to arch-rivals Barcelona on a free transfer, becoming a crowd hero and eventually captaining the club.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after eight seasons at Barcelona, having played 558 official games and scored 144 goals across his career.

trajectory.title: FC Barcelona head coach
trajectory.description: Appointed head coach of FC Barcelona, leading the team to a treble (La Liga, Copa del Rey, Champions League) in his first season with the Messi-Suárez-Neymar forward line.

trajectory.title: PSG head coach
trajectory.description: Appointed head coach of Paris Saint-Germain, continuing his career at the highest level of European football management.

name: Dražen Petrović
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Champions Cup (EuroLeague) with Cibona Zagreb in 1985 at age 20, scoring 36 points in the final against Real Madrid, and repeated as EuroLeague champion in 1986; named FIBA World Championship MVP in 1986 and Best Athlete of Yugoslavia in 1985.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Šibenik, SR Croatia, SFR Yugoslavia, to a basketball-loving family; he joined the local club Šibenka's senior team at age 15 and was known for his obsessive work ethic and scoring ability.
current_position: Died June 7, 1993, at age 28 in a car accident in Denkendorf, Germany; final role: starting shooting guard for the New Jersey Nets, averaging 22.3 points per game in his final season.

trajectory.title: Birth in Šibenik, Yugoslavia
trajectory.description: Born October 22, 1964, in Šibenik, SR Croatia, SFR Yugoslavia; joined BC Šibenka's senior team at age 15 and developed an obsessive work ethic that defined his career.

trajectory.title: Šibenka and Korać Cup finals
trajectory.description: Played in two Radivoj Korać Cup finals with Šibenka (1982 and 1983), establishing himself as one of Yugoslavia's most promising young players.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Cibona Zagreb
trajectory.description: Signed for BC Cibona Zagreb, where he would achieve his greatest European success and become a basketball legend.

trajectory.title: EuroLeague champion with Cibona
trajectory.description: Won the European Champions Cup (EuroLeague) with Cibona, scoring 36 points in the final against Real Madrid, and was named Best Athlete of Yugoslavia.

trajectory.title: Second EuroLeague and FIBA World Championship MVP
trajectory.description: Repeated as EuroLeague champion with Cibona and was named MVP of the FIBA World Championship, cementing his status as Europe's best player.

trajectory.title: NBA debut with Portland Trail Blazers
trajectory.description: Joined the NBA with the Portland Trail Blazers, becoming the first Croatian to play in the NBA, though he initially struggled for playing time.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with New Jersey Nets
trajectory.description: Traded to the New Jersey Nets and experienced a breakthrough, becoming one of the league's best shooting guards and averaging over 20 points per game.

trajectory.title: Death in car accident
trajectory.description: Died June 7, 1993, at age 28 in a car accident on a German highway, cutting short a career that was reaching its peak; inducted posthumously into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2002.

name: Carlos Sainz
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Spanish Rally Championship in 1987 at age 25 with a Ford Sierra RS Cosworth, and successfully defended the title in 1988 at age 26, while also making his first World Rally Championship appearances in 1987 with Ford.
starting_point: Born in 1962 in Madrid, Spain; he gave up a law degree to focus on motorsport, starting rallying in 1980 and winning the inaugural SEAT Copa Panda one-make series in 1981.
current_position: Retired Spanish rally driver; four-time Dakar Rally winner; two-time World Rally Champion; continues to compete in rally raids; resides in Spain.

trajectory.title: Birth in Madrid
trajectory.description: Born April 12, 1962, in Madrid, Spain; gave up a law degree to pursue motorsport full-time, beginning rallying in 1980.

trajectory.title: First rally championship
trajectory.description: Won the inaugural SEAT Copa Panda one-make rally series, launching his professional rallying career.

trajectory.title: Spanish Rally Championship title
trajectory.description: Won the Spanish Rally Championship with a Ford Sierra RS Cosworth and made his first World Rally Championship appearances with Ford.

trajectory.title: Defended Spanish Rally Championship
trajectory.description: Successfully defended the Spanish Rally Championship title, while continuing to gain experience in WRC events.

trajectory.title: First World Rally Championship title
trajectory.description: Won the World Rally Championship drivers' title with Toyota, becoming the first Spanish driver to win the WRC.

trajectory.title: Second WRC title
trajectory.description: Won his second World Rally Championship drivers' title with Toyota, solidifying his status as one of rallying's all-time greats.

trajectory.title: First Dakar Rally victory
trajectory.description: Won the Dakar Rally for the first time with Volkswagen, becoming the only Spaniard to win the event in the car category.

trajectory.title: Fourth Dakar Rally victory
trajectory.description: Won his fourth Dakar Rally with Audi, becoming the first driver to win with a hybrid-powered car and achieving victories with four different manufacturers.

name: Salvatore Garau
milestone_by_age_26: Became the drummer of the Italian progressive rock group Stormy Six in 1977 at age 23-24, performing on the critically noted album 'L'Apprendista' (1977), which was well received in progressive rock circles and released on the L'Orchestra label.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Santa Giusta, on the island of Sardinia, Italy; he studied at the Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze, graduating in 1974, before pursuing a career in music.
current_position: Italian visual artist and former musician; works as a painter and video artist; has exhibited internationally including at the Venice Biennale; resides in Italy.

trajectory.title: Birth in Santa Giusta, Sardinia
trajectory.description: Born in 1953 in Santa Giusta, in the province of Oristano on the Mediterranean island of Sardinia, Italy.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Academy of Fine Arts Florence
trajectory.description: Graduated from the Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze in 1974, having developed skills in both visual arts and music.

trajectory.title: Drummer of Stormy Six
trajectory.description: Became the drummer of the Italian progressive rock group Stormy Six in 1977, performing on the critically noted album 'L'Apprendista' released on the L'Orchestra label.

trajectory.title: Return to visual arts
trajectory.description: Began feeling a strong pull toward painting again, gradually transitioning from music to visual art while still performing concerts with Stormy Six.

trajectory.title: First solo art exhibition
trajectory.description: Held his first solo show in Milan in 1984, marking the official launch of his career as a visual artist after Stormy Six disbanded.

trajectory.title: Venice Biennale participation
trajectory.description: Participated in the 50th Biennale di Venezia and showed work at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, establishing his international reputation as a visual artist.

trajectory.title: Novel debut
trajectory.description: Published his debut novel 'Crudele amore mio' with Newton & Compton, expanding his creative output to literature.

name: Kim Kyong-il
milestone_by_age_26: Selected to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup at age 22, and represented North Korea at the 2005 FIFA U-17 World Championship and 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup.
starting_point: Born in 1988 in Pyongyang, North Korea; he grew up in the North Korean football system, joining Rimyongsu club in the DPR Korea League from a young age.
current_position: North Korean international footballer; plays for Rimyongsu in the DPR Korea League; current status not widely documented in international media.

trajectory.title: Birth in Pyongyang
trajectory.description: Born December 11, 1988, in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the North Korean football system.

trajectory.title: FIFA U-17 World Championship
trajectory.description: Represented North Korea at the 2005 FIFA U-17 World Championship in Peru, scoring two goals in four matches and showcasing his talent on the youth international stage.

trajectory.title: FIFA U-20 World Cup and senior debut
trajectory.description: Played in three matches at the 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Canada and made his senior national team debut on October 21, 2007, in a World Cup qualification match against Mongolia.

trajectory.title: AFC Challenge Cup
trajectory.description: Represented North Korea at the 2008 AFC Challenge Cup, appearing in five matches as part of the national team's buildup to World Cup qualification.

trajectory.title: 2010 FIFA World Cup squad
trajectory.description: Selected to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966, though he did not play in the tournament.

name: Kim Myong-gil
milestone_by_age_26: Named to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup at age 25, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966, having represented the national team in World Cup qualifiers from 2005.
starting_point: Born in 1984 in Pyongyang, North Korea; he grew up in the North Korean football system and played as a goalkeeper for April 25 Sports Club, a military-linked team in the DPR Korea Premier Football League.
current_position: North Korean international footballer; plays as a goalkeeper; current status not widely documented in international media.

trajectory.title: Birth in Pyongyang
trajectory.description: Born October 16, 1984, in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the North Korean football system as a goalkeeper.

trajectory.title: National team debut and World Cup qualifiers
trajectory.description: Began representing North Korea in 2006 World Cup qualifying campaigns from 2005, appearing in multiple matches including against Bahrain, Iran, and Japan.

trajectory.title: EAFF East Asian Cup
trajectory.description: Represented North Korea at the 2005 EAFF East Asian Cup, appearing in matches against Japan and South Korea.

trajectory.title: 2010 FIFA World Cup squad
trajectory.description: Named to North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966, as a backup goalkeeper.

trajectory.title: Continued international career
trajectory.description: Continued representing North Korea in 2014 World Cup qualifying matches, appearing against Tajikistan in September 2011.

name: Klaus Ebner
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Großer Österreichischer Jugendpreis (Austrian Youth Prize for Literature) in 1982 at age 18 for the novella 'Das Brandmal,' and again in 1988 for the novel 'Nils,' establishing early recognition as a literary talent.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Vienna, Austria, to a middle-class family; his mother was a hairdresser and his father a salesman who sold home entertainment products. He began writing at age twelve, composing a short theater play with school friends.
current_position: Austrian writer, essayist, poet, and translator living in Vienna; writes in German and Catalan; member of several Austrian writers' associations including the Grazer Autorenversammlung.

trajectory.title: Birth in Vienna
trajectory.description: Born August 8, 1964, in Vienna, Austria, to a hairdresser mother and salesman father; began writing at age twelve with a short theater play rehearsed with school friends.

trajectory.title: Austrian Youth Prize for Literature
trajectory.description: Won the Großer Österreichischer Jugendpreis (Austrian Youth Prize for Literature) for the novella 'Das Brandmal,' establishing early recognition as a literary talent.

trajectory.title: University studies in Vienna
trajectory.description: Began studying Romance languages, German philology, and translation at the University of Vienna after a university trip to Tours, France.

trajectory.title: Second Austrian Youth Prize
trajectory.description: Won the Austrian Youth Prize for Literature again, this time for the novel 'Nils,' confirming his status as a promising young writer.

trajectory.title: IT writing career begins
trajectory.description: Began publishing articles and books on software topics, eventually publishing nine IT books through 2004 while pursuing freelance translation work.

trajectory.title: Wiener Werkstattpreis
trajectory.description: Won the Wiener Werkstattpreis (main prize) for short story and essay, marking a return to literary recognition after years focused on IT writing.

trajectory.title: Publication of Hominide
trajectory.description: Published the short novel 'Hominide,' a significant literary work that expanded his reputation as a prose writer.

trajectory.title: Catalan poetry prize
trajectory.description: Won the Premi de Poesia Parc Taulí, a Catalan poetry prize, for his collection 'Blaus/Bläuen,' reflecting his bilingual literary output in German and Catalan.

name: Didier Pironi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Formula Renault Eurocup in 1974 at age 22, then won the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1978 at age 26 and made his Formula One debut the same year.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Villecresnes, Val-de-Marne, France, into a family with motorsport connections; his half-brother José Dolhem was a racing driver, and Pironi initially studied engineering before enrolling at the Winfield Racing School at Paul Ricard.
current_position: Died August 23, 1987, at age 35 in a powerboat racing accident off the Isle of Wight, England; final role: retired F1 driver and offshore powerboat racer.

trajectory.title: Birth in Villecresnes, France
trajectory.description: Born March 26, 1952, in Villecresnes, Val-de-Marne, France; his half-brother José Dolhem was a racing driver who influenced his early interest in motorsport.

trajectory.title: Elf driving school scholarship
trajectory.description: Enrolled in the Elf driving school at Paul Ricard, winning the 'Volant Elf' scholarship that provided financial support for a racing programme.

trajectory.title: Formula Renault Eurocup champion
trajectory.description: Won the Formula Renault Eurocup, establishing himself as one of France's most promising young racing drivers alongside René Arnoux and Patrick Tambay.

trajectory.title: Monaco F3 and European F2 success
trajectory.description: Won the Monaco Formula 3 Grand Prix and finished third in the European Formula Two Championship, earning a promotion to Formula One.

trajectory.title: Le Mans victory and F1 debut
trajectory.description: Won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Renault alongside Jean-Pierre Jaussaud, and made his Formula One debut with Tyrrell at the Argentine Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory with Ligier
trajectory.description: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 1980 Belgian Grand Prix with Ligier, finishing fifth in the championship with several podiums.

trajectory.title: Championship runner-up and career-ending crash
trajectory.description: Was leading the 1982 World Championship with Ferrari when a horrific crash during qualifying for the German Grand Prix severely injured his legs, ending his F1 career; lost the title by 5 points to Keke Rosberg.

trajectory.title: Death in powerboat accident
trajectory.description: Died August 23, 1987, at age 35 in a powerboat racing accident off the Isle of Wight, England, while competing in offshore powerboat racing.

name: Pak Sung-hyok
milestone_by_age_26: Selected for the North Korea 2010 FIFA World Cup squad at age 20, having debuted for the national team in 2009 at age 19.
starting_point: Born in 1990 in Pyongyang, North Korea; he developed through the North Korean football system, playing for Sobaeksu in the DPR Korea League.
current_position: North Korean international footballer; plays for Sobaeksu in the DPR Korea League; current status not widely documented in international media.

trajectory.title: Birth in Pyongyang
trajectory.description: Born May 30, 1990, in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the North Korean football system from a young age, joining the Sobaeksu youth setup.

trajectory.title: National team debut
trajectory.description: Debuted for the North Korean national team in 2009, appearing in East Asian Championship qualifying matches against Chinese Taipei, Hong Kong, and Guam.

trajectory.title: 2010 FIFA World Cup squad
trajectory.description: Selected for North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa at age 20, the country's first World Cup appearance since 1966.

trajectory.title: Post-World Cup career
trajectory.description: Continued playing for Sobaeksu in the DPR Korea League following the 2010 World Cup, maintaining his place in the national team pool for subsequent qualifying campaigns.

trajectory.title: AFC Challenge Cup participation
trajectory.description: Was part of North Korea's squad during the 2012 AFC Challenge Cup qualifying rounds, continuing to represent his country in regional competitions.

name: Pak Chol-jin
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for the North Korea national football team in 2003 at age 18, played in multiple World Cup qualifying campaigns, and was selected for the 2010 FIFA World Cup squad at age 25.
starting_point: Born in 1985 in Pyongyang, North Korea; he developed through the North Korean football system as a defender, playing club football in the DPR Korea League.
current_position: North Korean international footballer; plays as a defender; current status not widely documented in international media.

trajectory.title: Birth in Pyongyang
trajectory.description: Born September 5, 1985, in Pyongyang, North Korea; developed through the North Korean football system as a centre-back.

trajectory.title: National team debut
trajectory.description: Debuted for the North Korea national football team in 2003 at age 18, beginning an international career spanning multiple World Cup qualifying campaigns.

trajectory.title: World Cup qualifying and East Asian Cup
trajectory.description: Represented North Korea in 2006 World Cup qualifying matches and the EAFF East Asian Cup, becoming a regular in the national team defense.

trajectory.title: 2010 World Cup qualifying campaign
trajectory.description: Was a key defender in North Korea's successful 2010 World Cup qualifying campaign, appearing in eight qualifying matches throughout 2008.

trajectory.title: 2010 FIFA World Cup squad
trajectory.description: Selected for North Korea's 23-man squad for the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, starting all three group matches against Brazil, Portugal, and Ivory Coast.

name: Ari Vatanen
milestone_by_age_26: Won the British Rally Championship in 1976 at age 24 driving a Ford Escort RS1800, and competed in the World Rally Championship from 1974.
starting_point: Born in 1952 in Tuupovaara, Finland, a rural municipality in eastern Finland; he began rallying in 1970 and made his WRC debut at the 1974 1000 Lakes Rally, quickly gaining attention by beating Hannu Mikkola in the Nortti Rally.
current_position: Retired Finnish rally driver and former politician; served as Member of the European Parliament (1999-2009); resides in France and Finland.

trajectory.title: Birth in Tuupovaara, Finland
trajectory.description: Born April 27, 1952, in Tuupovaara, Finland; began rallying in 1970 and made his WRC debut at the 1974 1000 Lakes Rally.

trajectory.title: WRC debut and early attention
trajectory.description: Debuted in the World Rally Championship at the 1974 1000 Lakes Rally and won the Nortti Rally in an Opel Ascona, beating the legendary Hannu Mikkola.

trajectory.title: British Rally Championship title
trajectory.description: Won the British Rally Championship driving a Ford Escort RS1800, establishing himself as a top-tier rally driver.

trajectory.title: First WRC podium
trajectory.description: Achieved his first WRC podium finish at the 1977 Rally New Zealand, demonstrating his potential at the highest level of the sport.

trajectory.title: First WRC victory
trajectory.description: Won his first World Rally Championship event at the 1980 Acropolis Rally, breaking through to the top level of international rallying.

trajectory.title: World Rally Champion
trajectory.description: Won the World Rally Championship drivers' title, the pinnacle of his rallying career, driving a Ford Escort RS1800 as a privateer.

trajectory.title: First Dakar Rally victory
trajectory.description: Won the Paris-Dakar Rally for the first time with Peugeot, beginning a remarkable second career in rally raid competition.

trajectory.title: European Parliament election
trajectory.description: Elected as a Member of the European Parliament for Finland, beginning a decade-long political career while maintaining connections to motorsport.

name: Filippo Inzaghi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Capocannoniere (Serie A top scorer) with 24 goals for Atalanta in the 1996-97 season at age 23, and was named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year, before transferring to Juventus and winning the Scudetto.
starting_point: Born in 1973 in Piacenza, Italy, to a footballing family; his younger brother Simone also became a professional footballer. He began his youth career at San Nicolò before joining Piacenza's academy in 1985.
current_position: Italian football manager; head coach of Serie B club Palermo; former striker who played for Juventus and AC Milan; resides in Italy.

trajectory.title: Birth in Piacenza
trajectory.description: Born August 9, 1973, in Piacenza, Italy; began his youth career at San Nicolò before joining Piacenza's academy in 1985, alongside his brother Simone.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Piacenza
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut with Piacenza, interspersed with loan spells at AlbinoLeffe and Verona where he developed his goal-scoring instincts.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Parma
trajectory.description: Joined Parma in Serie A, marking his entrance into top-flight Italian football, though he scored only 4 goals in 22 appearances.

trajectory.title: Capocannoniere with Atalanta
trajectory.description: Won the Capocannoniere (Serie A top scorer) with 24 goals for Atalanta in the 1996-97 season and was named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Juventus and Scudetto
trajectory.description: Transferred to Juventus and won the Scudetto in his first season, scoring 18 goals and forming a prolific partnership with Alessandro Del Piero.

trajectory.title: Move to AC Milan
trajectory.description: Joined AC Milan at the peak of his career, where he would spend 11 seasons and become a club legend.

trajectory.title: Champions League title with Milan
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League with AC Milan, the first of two Champions League titles (2003 and 2007) with the Rossoneri.

trajectory.title: Champions League final heroics
trajectory.description: Scored both goals in the 2007 Champions League final against Liverpool, cementing his legacy as one of Europe's greatest clutch goal-scorers with 46 Champions League goals.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after 11 seasons at AC Milan, having scored 313 goals in official matches and won two Champions League titles and three Serie A titles.

name: Gerhard Berger
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut at the 1984 Austrian Grand Prix at age 24 driving for ATS, and secured a full-season F1 drive with Arrows in 1985, establishing himself as an F1 driver by age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1959 in Wörgl, Austria, to a family that owned a truck company; his father Johann owned the business where Gerhard worked before being promoted to driver, and he progressed through Formula Ford and European Formula Three.
current_position: Retired Austrian racing driver and motorsport executive; served as BMW's motorsport director; resides in Austria; won 10 F1 Grands Prix across 14 seasons.

trajectory.title: Birth in Wörgl, Austria
trajectory.description: Born August 27, 1959, in Wörgl, Austria; his father owned a truck company where Gerhard worked before pursuing motorsport through Formula Ford and European Formula Three.

trajectory.title: Formula One debut with ATS
trajectory.description: Made his Formula One debut at the 1984 Austrian Grand Prix driving for ATS, finishing 12th on his home circuit and scoring points at Monza in his second race.

trajectory.title: Full-season F1 drive with Arrows
trajectory.description: Secured a full-season F1 drive with Arrows in 1985, scoring his first championship points with a fifth-place finish at the South African Grand Prix.

trajectory.title: First F1 victory with Benetton
trajectory.description: Joined Benetton and won his first Grand Prix at the 1986 Mexican Grand Prix, exploiting the power of the BMW turbo engine and clever Pirelli tyre strategy.

trajectory.title: Ferrari contract and multiple wins
trajectory.description: Signed a three-year contract with Ferrari on the strength of his Benetton performances, winning the Japanese and Australian Grands Prix in 1987.

trajectory.title: Move to McLaren alongside Senna
trajectory.description: Joined McLaren as teammate to Ayrton Senna, contributing to the team's 1990 and 1991 constructors' titles and forming a close friendship with the Brazilian legend.

trajectory.title: Retirement from Formula One
trajectory.description: Retired from Formula One at the end of the 1997 season with 10 wins, 12 pole positions, 21 fastest laps, and 48 podiums across 210 Grand Prix starts over 14 seasons.

name: Mohammed Ben Sulayem
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first FIA Middle East Rally Championship title in 1986 at age 24, becoming the UAE's first motor-racing champion. By age 26 he had won two consecutive MERC titles (1986 and 1987).
starting_point: Born in 1961 in Dubai, Trucial States (now UAE), into a wealthy family; his brother Sultan Ahmed became chairman of Dubai Port World. He studied business at the American University in Washington, D.C. before pursuing rallying.
current_position: President of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) since December 2021; re-elected for a second term in December 2025; the first non-European to hold the position.

trajectory.title: Birth in Dubai
trajectory.description: Born November 12, 1961, in Dubai, Trucial States (now United Arab Emirates), into a wealthy family; studied business at the American University in Washington, D.C.

trajectory.title: Rally career begins
trajectory.description: Began his rally driving career in the early 1980s, competing in the Middle East Rally Championship and winning international events.

trajectory.title: First Middle East Rally Championship title
trajectory.description: Won his first FIA Middle East Rally Championship title with a Toyota Celica, becoming the UAE's first motor-racing champion.

trajectory.title: Second consecutive MERC title
trajectory.description: Successfully defended his Middle East Rally Championship title, beginning a run of six consecutive titles through 1991.

trajectory.title: Seventh MERC title with Ford
trajectory.description: Won his seventh Middle East Rally Championship title with a Ford Escort RS Cosworth, continuing his dominance of regional rallying.

trajectory.title: Retirement from competitive driving
trajectory.description: Retired from competitive rallying with a record 14 Middle East Rally Championship titles and 61 international event victories, the most successful driver in MERC history.

trajectory.title: President of Emirates Motorsports Organization
trajectory.description: Became President of the Emirates Motorsports Organization (EMSO), representing the UAE in the FIA and beginning his transition from driver to administrator.

trajectory.title: Elected FIA President
trajectory.description: Elected as President of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), succeeding Jean Todt and becoming the first non-European to hold the position.

name: Rudi Völler
milestone_by_age_26: Became Bundesliga top scorer with 23 goals for Werder Bremen in the 1982-83 season at age 23, was named German Footballer of the Year in 1983, and earned his first cap for West Germany in 1982.
starting_point: Born in 1960 in Hanau, West Germany, to a footballing family; he began playing in his father's team at age eight and signed with Kickers Offenbach at 17, weighing only 65kg and earning the nickname 'Beanpole.'
current_position: Director of the Germany national team; former professional footballer and manager; resides in Germany; one of the most respected figures in German football.

trajectory.title: Birth in Hanau, West Germany
trajectory.description: Born April 13, 1960, in Hanau, West Germany; began playing football in his father's team at age eight before signing with Kickers Offenbach at 17.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Kickers Offenbach
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut with Kickers Offenbach in Germany's second tier, earning the nickname 'Beanpole' due to his slender frame.

trajectory.title: Move to 1860 Munich
trajectory.description: Transferred to 1860 Munich, where he endured a tough relegation season but became the driving force behind the club's promotion with 37 goals the following year.

trajectory.title: Werder Bremen and West Germany debut
trajectory.description: Signed for Werder Bremen, earned his first cap for West Germany, and became Bundesliga top scorer with 23 goals in the 1982-83 season, also named German Footballer of the Year.

trajectory.title: World Cup runner-up with West Germany
trajectory.description: Was a key member of West Germany's 1986 World Cup squad that reached the final, scoring in the tournament despite suffering injuries during the season.

trajectory.title: Transfer to AS Roma
trajectory.description: Moved to AS Roma in Serie A, where he won the Coppa Italia and was runner-up in the UEFA Cup, becoming a fan favorite known as 'Il tedesco volante' (The Flying German).

trajectory.title: World Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won the 1990 World Cup with West Germany, scoring three goals in the tournament and forming a successful strike partnership with Jürgen Klinsmann.

trajectory.title: Champions League with Marseille
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League with Olympique Marseille in the 1992-93 season, though the club's league title was later stripped due to a match-fixing scandal.

name: Cha Bum-kun
