milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest player in the world to reach 100 international caps at age 24 in 1978, won Asian Games gold medal in 1978, and signed with Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga in July 1979 at age 26, later winning the UEFA Cup in 1980.
starting_point: Born in 1953 in Hwaseong, South Korea, to a family that valued sports; he attended Kyungshin Middle School and Kyungshin High School before joining Korea University, where he developed into a top striker and debuted for South Korea at 18.
current_position: Retired South Korean footballer and manager; widely regarded as the greatest Asian footballer of all time; resides in South Korea; named IFFHS Asia's Player of the Century.

trajectory.title: Birth in Hwaseong, South Korea
trajectory.description: Born May 22, 1953, in Hwaseong, South Korea; attended Kyungshin schools before joining Korea University, where he developed into a top striker.

trajectory.title: Youngest South Korea debutant
trajectory.description: Became the youngest-ever debutant for South Korea's senior national team at age 18, scoring his first international goal in the 1972 AFC Asian Cup.

trajectory.title: Korean FA Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Voted the best player in South Korea at age 20, having been named to the Korean FA Best XI for the first time in 1972, a feat he repeated for seven straight years.

trajectory.title: 100 international caps and Asian Games gold
trajectory.description: Became the youngest player in the world to reach 100 international caps at age 24, and won a gold medal at the 1978 Asian Games.

trajectory.title: Bundesliga move to Eintracht Frankfurt
trajectory.description: Signed with Eintracht Frankfurt in July 1979, becoming the first South Korean to play in the Bundesliga and beginning a trailblazing European career.

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup with Eintracht Frankfurt
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Cup with Eintracht Frankfurt in 1980, becoming one of the first Asian players to win a major European club trophy.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Bayer Leverkusen
trajectory.description: Moved to Bayer Leverkusen, where he spent six seasons and scored 52 goals in 185 Bundesliga matches, becoming the Bundesliga's all-time foreign top scorer (98 goals) until 1999.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football in 1989 after a decade in the Bundesliga, later named IFFHS Asia's Player of the Century and inducted into the Korean FA Hall of Fame.

name: Bonnie Tyler
milestone_by_age_26: Her debut single 'Lost in France' reached #9 on the UK singles chart in 1976 at age 25, and her debut album 'The World Starts Tonight' was released in February 1977, both before her 26th birthday in June 1977.
starting_point: Born in 1951 in Skewen, Wales, to a coal miner's family in a council house with an outside toilet; she grew up with three sisters and two brothers, loving music and performing in pubs and clubs around South Wales for seven years before being discovered.
current_position: Welsh singer with a 50-year career; awarded MBE in 2023 for services to music; continues to perform; resides in Wales.

trajectory.title: Birth in Skewen, Wales
trajectory.description: Born Gaynor Hopkins on June 8, 1951, in Skewen, Wales, a coal miner's daughter growing up in public housing with an outside toilet and five siblings.

trajectory.title: Talent contest and early performances
trajectory.description: Entered a local talent competition at her aunt's insistence, placing second, and was inspired to pursue singing, performing as a backing singer before forming her own band Imagination.

trajectory.title: RCA recording contract
trajectory.description: Spotted by talent scout Roger Bell singing in the Townsman Club in Swansea, was brought to London and signed by RCA Records, adopting the stage name Bonnie Tyler.

trajectory.title: 'Lost in France' hits UK Top 10
trajectory.description: Released 'Lost in France' which peaked at #9 on the UK singles chart, leading to her first appearance on Top of the Pops and establishing her recording career.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'The World Starts Tonight'
trajectory.description: Released her debut studio album 'The World Starts Tonight' in February 1977, followed by the hit single 'It's a Heartache' in 1978 which reached #3 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

trajectory.title: 'Total Eclipse of the Heart' global hit
trajectory.description: Released 'Total Eclipse of the Heart' which topped the UK charts and reached #4 in the US, becoming one of the most iconic power ballads of all time and later surpassing a billion streams on Spotify.

trajectory.title: Eurovision Song Contest
trajectory.description: Represented the United Kingdom at the 2013 Eurovision Song Contest with 'Believe in Me,' maintaining her public profile across Europe.

trajectory.title: MBE for services to music
trajectory.description: Awarded an MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours list for her services to music, presented by Prince William, and published her autobiography 'Straight from the Heart.'

name: Adrian Smith
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Iron Maiden in November 1980 at age 23 and recorded on 'The Number of the Beast' (1982), which reached #1 on the UK albums chart and became one of the most influential heavy metal albums of all time, all before turning 26 in February 1983.
starting_point: Born in 1957 in Hackney, London, England, to a working-class family; his father was a painter and decorator from Homerton. He grew up in Clapton and became interested in rock music at 15, forming a friendship with future Iron Maiden guitarist Dave Murray.
current_position: English guitarist and singer; member of Iron Maiden (second tenure since 1999); also leads side projects including Smith/Kotzen; resides in England.

trajectory.title: Birth in Hackney, London
trajectory.description: Born February 27, 1957, in Hackney, London; his father was a painter and decorator. He grew up in Clapton and became interested in rock music at 15 after buying Deep Purple's Machine Head.

trajectory.title: Formed band with Dave Murray
trajectory.description: Formed a band called Stone Free with neighborhood friend Dave Murray, who inspired him to take up guitar, starting with an old Spanish guitar before buying Murray's old guitar for £5.

trajectory.title: Founded and led Urchin
trajectory.description: Formed the band Urchin after leaving school at 16, leading the group until their demise in 1980 and developing his songwriting and guitar skills.

trajectory.title: Joined Iron Maiden
trajectory.description: Joined Iron Maiden in November 1980, replacing Dennis Stratton and beginning a partnership with Dave Murray that would define the band's twin-guitar sound.

trajectory.title: 'The Number of the Beast' #1 album
trajectory.description: Recorded on 'The Number of the Beast' (1982), which reached #1 on the UK albums chart and became one of the most influential heavy metal albums of all time.

trajectory.title: 'Piece of Mind' and global success
trajectory.description: Recorded on 'Piece of Mind' (1983), continuing Iron Maiden's rise to global metal dominance with subsequent albums including 'Powerslave' (1984) and 'Seventh Son of a Seventh Son' (1988).

trajectory.title: Departure from Iron Maiden
trajectory.description: Left Iron Maiden in 1990 after the No Prayer for the Dying sessions, pursuing solo projects including ASAP and later forming Psycho Motel.

trajectory.title: Return to Iron Maiden
trajectory.description: Returned to Iron Maiden in 1999 alongside Bruce Dickinson, rejoining the band for a highly successful second tenure that continues to the present day with a three-guitar lineup.

name: Eros Ramazzotti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Sanremo Music Festival main competition in 1986 at age 22 with 'Adesso tu,' having already won the Newcomers' category in 1984 and released a debut album with multi-million-selling singles across Europe by 1985.
starting_point: Born in 1963 in Cinecittà Est, a suburb of Rome, Italy, to a working-class family; his father was a construction worker and amateur musician who encouraged his musical development, and he grew up in a public housing complex.
current_position: Italian pop and rock singer-songwriter with over 80 million records sold worldwide; continues to record and tour; resides in Italy; one of the most successful Italian artists of all time.

trajectory.title: Birth in Cinecittà, Rome
trajectory.description: Born October 28, 1963, in Cinecittà Est, a suburb of Rome, to a construction worker father and housewife mother; grew up in the Lamaro public housing complex and began playing guitar at age seven.

trajectory.title: Castrocaro competition and first contract
trajectory.description: Participated in the Voci Nuove di Castrocaro competition with 'Rock 80,' reaching the final and receiving a recording contract with DDD label, moving to Milan.

trajectory.title: Sanremo Newcomers' win
trajectory.description: Won the Sanremo Music Festival Newcomers' category with 'Terra promessa,' which became a breakout hit single and launched his recording career.

trajectory.title: Debut album 'Cuori agitati'
trajectory.description: Released his debut album 'Cuori agitati' featuring the hit single 'Una storia importante,' which became his first international hit, particularly in France.

trajectory.title: Sanremo main competition win
trajectory.description: Won the Sanremo Music Festival main competition with 'Adesso tu' and released the album 'Nuovi eroi,' solidifying his status as a major Italian pop star.

trajectory.title: Radio City Music Hall debut
trajectory.description: Invited by Clive Davis to perform at Radio City Music Hall in New York, becoming the first Italian artist to sell out the venue, marking his international breakthrough.

trajectory.title: 'Tutte storie' global success
trajectory.description: Released 'Tutte storie' which achieved record-breaking sales, with the single 'Cose della vita' (video directed by Spike Lee) becoming a global hit.

trajectory.title: 'Eros' compilation with major duets
trajectory.description: Released the compilation album 'Eros' featuring duets with Tina Turner and Andrea Bocelli, further expanding his international audience and cementing his status as a global star.

name: Pavel Nedvěd
milestone_by_age_26: Was a key player in Czech Republic's run to the Euro 1996 final at age 23-24, scoring against Italy, and transferred to Serie A club Lazio in 1996 after winning three league titles with Sparta Prague.
starting_point: Born in 1972 in Cheb, Czechoslovakia, to a family that nurtured his football development; he began playing at a very young age with TJ Skalná before moving through RH Cheb and Škoda Plzeň's youth systems.
current_position: Czech former professional footballer; serves as general director of the Czech national team and under-21s; formerly Vice President of Juventus (2015-2022); resides in the Czech Republic.

trajectory.title: Birth in Cheb, Czechoslovakia
trajectory.description: Born August 30, 1972, in Cheb, Czechoslovakia; began playing football at a very young age with TJ Skalná before moving to RH Cheb and then Škoda Plzeň.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Škoda Plzeň
trajectory.description: Began his senior career at Škoda Plzeň, was loaned to Dukla Prague in 1991, and then signed for Sparta Prague in 1992.

trajectory.title: Three league titles with Sparta Prague
trajectory.description: Won three consecutive Czech league titles with Sparta Prague (1992-93, 1993-94, 1994-95) and two Czech Cups, establishing himself as one of the country's best players.

trajectory.title: Euro 96 final and Lazio transfer
trajectory.description: Was a key player in Czech Republic's run to the Euro 1996 final, scoring the winning goal against Italy, and transferred to Serie A club Lazio for a significant fee.

trajectory.title: Cup Winners' Cup with Lazio
trajectory.description: Won the last-ever Cup Winners' Cup with Lazio, one of the club's greatest achievements, and became a fan favorite for his tireless midfield performances.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Juventus
trajectory.description: Transferred to Juventus to replace Zinedine Zidane, becoming a fundamental player for the club over eight seasons.

trajectory.title: Ballon d'Or winner
trajectory.description: Won the Ballon d'Or as European Footballer of the Year, becoming the second Czech player to win the award and leading Juventus to the Champions League final.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after the 2008-09 season, having played 501 league matches and been capped 91 times for the Czech Republic, scoring 18 international goals.

name: The Undertaker
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WWF Championship at Survivor Series on November 27, 1991 at age 26, defeating Hulk Hogan to become the youngest WWF Champion in history at that point.
starting_point: Born in 1965 in Houston, Texas, to Frank and Betty Calaway, one of five brothers; he grew up playing sports including basketball at Texas Wesleyan University before dropping out to pursue professional wrestling, training under Buzz Sawyer in the mid-1980s.
current_position: Retired American professional wrestler; signed to WWE as a brand ambassador; inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2022; resides in Texas.

trajectory.title: Birth in Houston, Texas
trajectory.description: Born Mark William Calaway on March 24, 1965, in Houston, Texas, one of five brothers; played basketball at Angelina College and Texas Wesleyan University before dropping out to pursue wrestling.

trajectory.title: Professional wrestling debut
trajectory.description: Debuted in 1987 in World Class Championship Wrestling (WCCW) as the masked 'Texas Red,' losing to Bruiser Brody, and worked various gimmicks across regional promotions.

trajectory.title: WCW as 'Mean Mark' Callous
trajectory.description: Signed with World Championship Wrestling (WCW) in 1989 as 'Mean' Mark Callous, teaming with Dan Spivey in The Skyscrapers and challenging Lex Luger for the US title.

trajectory.title: WWF debut as The Undertaker
trajectory.description: Joined the World Wrestling Federation (WWF) in November 1990 at Survivor Series, debuting as The Undertaker — a macabre 'Deadman' character that would become one of wrestling's most iconic gimmicks.

trajectory.title: WWF Championship at Survivor Series
trajectory.description: Won the WWF Championship at Survivor Series on November 27, 1991, defeating Hulk Hogan to become the youngest WWF Champion in history at that point.

trajectory.title: First Hell in a Cell match
trajectory.description: Participated in the inaugural Hell in a Cell match at Badd Blood in October 1997 against Shawn Michaels, one of the most influential matches in wrestling history.

trajectory.title: Royal Rumble winner
trajectory.description: Won the Royal Rumble match in 2007, entering at #30 and last eliminating Shawn Michaels, adding another major achievement to his legendary career.

trajectory.title: The Streak broken at WrestleMania 30
trajectory.description: Had his legendary 21-0 WrestleMania winning streak broken by Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 30, one of the most shocking moments in wrestling history.

trajectory.title: Final match and retirement
trajectory.description: Had his final match at WrestleMania 36 in a Boneyard match against AJ Styles, officially retiring from in-ring competition after a 30-year career.

trajectory.title: WWE Hall of Fame induction
trajectory.description: Inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame by Vince McMahon, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest and most iconic professional wrestlers of all time.
